newsitem.title: USA: Reebok sees gross margins flat in '97.
newsitem.headline: Reebok sees gross margins flat in '97.

text.p: Reebok International Ltd Chief Financial Officer Kenneth Watchmaker said Thursday he expects gross margins in 1997 to stay at about the same level as in 1996, but rise over the long term.

Gross margins slipped in 1996 to 38.6 percent from 40.0 percent in 1995 due to the launch of new products and the impact of growth of Reebok's apparel business, which has lower margins, he told analysts and reporters on a conference call.
"I expect our 1997 gross margins to be about the same as in 1996," he said.
But over the long term, gross margins should rise as footwear is priced at higher levels and apparel margins rise to the level of the footwear margins, Watchmaker said.
Bob Meers, vice president in charge of the Reebok brand, said that based on strong new product and growth of the brand name, he expected to "see a slow increase in business throughout 1997."

Meers said Reebok's inventories are in "excellent shape" following problems in 1995, the overall operation is more efficient, and the company has secured additional production capacity to accomodate increased demand.
"Operationally, I'm more confident that surprises are behind us," he said.

Watchmaker repeated that the board of directors has the authorization to buy back Reebok shares, as the company has aggressively done over the past few years, but the company does not expect to be making any open market repurchases in the near term. Reebok will instead focus on paying down its debt, he said.
